paper.title: Finite-Horizon Single-Pull Restless Bandits: An Efficient Index Policy For Scarce Resource Allocation

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Planning problem for restless bandits with known MDPs (Markovian arms); no learning; restless/Markov settings are out of scope in v0.5.
unmapped: Each arm is a known finite-state MDP (planning, transition kernels and rewards known to the decision maker)
At most K arms activated per round (hard activation budget) and each arm can be pulled at most once (single-pull constraint)
Asymptotic regime: N classes of arms each replicated rho times, budget rho*K
Optimality gap is measured against the optimal policy, normalised per arm
settings.definition_quote:
\texttt{SPRMAB}:~~&\max_{\pi}\mathbb{E}_\pi \left(\sum_{n=1}^{N} \sum_{t=1}^{T} r_n(t)\right)\\
&\quad\mbox{s.t.}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\! a_n(t)\leq K,\forall t\in [T], ~\sum_{t=1}^T a_n(t)\leq 1, \forall n.

algorithms.name: Single-Pull Index (SPI) policy
requires_knowledge_of: transition kernels and reward functions of all arms

bound.expression_latex: \lim_{\rho\rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{\rho N}\Big(J^{\pi^{Opt}}(\rho K, \rho N)- J^{\pi^{SPI}}(\rho K, \rho N)\Big)=0

symbols.rho: scaling factor: number of arms per class

conditions: N classes of arms each replicated rho times, budget rho*K

source.label: thm:asym_opt
source.quote: The designed \texttt{SPI} policy (Algorithm~\ref{alg:Index}) is asymptotically optimal, i.e., \lim_{\rho\rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{\rho N}\Big(J^{\pi^{Opt}}(\rho K, \rho N)- J^{\pi^{SPI}}(\rho K, \rho N)\Big)=0.

results.notes: Asymptotic optimality of per-arm average optimality gap as rho -> infinity; planning problem with known MDPs. Proof only sketched with reference to prior work.

bound.regime: finite rho > 0, with probability at least 1 - 1/rho

symbols.rho: scaling factor: number of arms per class

conditions: N_cls classes of arms each replicated rho times, budget rho*K (paper writes rho*B)
Hellinger integral between joint and product reward distributions assumed to scale as rho^{-beta}, beta >= 0 (stated in proof)

source.label: thm:non-asymptotic
source.quote: For a finite number of $\rho\in\mathbb{R}^+$, with probability at least $1-\frac{1}{\rho}$ such that the average gap between the performance achieved by our index policy $ \pi^{Index}$ and the optimal policy $\pi^{SPI}$ is given as \frac{1}{\rho N}\Big(J^{\pi^{Opt}}(\rho B, \rho N)- J^{\pi^{SPI}}(\rho B, \rho N)\Big)\leq 2r_{\text{max}}T\sqrt{\frac{ \ln 2\rho}{2N\rho}}+5r_{\text{max}}T\sqrt{\frac{\ln 2\rho}{2\rho^3}}.

results.notes: Bound on per-arm average optimality gap (total gap divided by rho*N). The statement is a probability-1-1/rho statement about a deterministic (expected) quantity, which is unusual; recorded as stated. Corollary 1 restates this as O(rho^{-1/2} + rho^{-3/2}). Proof relies on questionable steps (assumed Hellinger scaling).
